hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
⬢ **This chat is at the plane root — in no workspace, on purpose.** purlis started it there (`$PURLIS_PLANE_ROOT_SESSION`), so do not ask the person which workspace to use and do not run `purlis workspace use`: this session stays at the root. From here you look after the plane itself — its personas, its settings, its memory — and its workspaces, which you may create, rename, curate or retire. Name the workspace on every command that acts on one, with `-w <name>` (`purlis ws todo -w <name> "<what>"`, `purlis workspace create <name> --vision "<the goal>"`); a command that needs a workspace and is not given one refuses rather than guess. Work inside a workspace's repos belongs in a chat started in that workspace.

⬢ **Unattended.** purlis started this chat with nobody at it, so no one answers a prompt or an ask: what needs a person is refused, not waited for.

⬢ **If work has to go to another chat.** Use purlis's tools for it first: `dispatch` starts a task; `dispatch_list`, `dispatch_read`, `dispatch_wait`, `dispatch_tell`, `dispatch_answer`, `dispatch_pass_on`, `dispatch_cancel` and `dispatch_close` look after one, and `dispatch_tell` with `all` tells every task still working at once; a task answers with `dispatch_note` (its `ack` acknowledges an instruction), `dispatch_ask` and `dispatch_report`. A task's question comes to you first: answer it, or pass it on with `dispatch_pass_on`. Security, cost, anything public and anything that amends a ruling are always passed on, and your own answer is never the person's word. They need no shell; the `purlis dispatch` command does the same, one call at a time. Work that writes, commits, needs its own branch folder or runs long is a purlis task, through `dispatch`; a harness's helper is for read-only work (searching, reading, reviewing), and from inside one `purlis worktree add`, `commit` and `push` are refused. Work this chat needs an answer from, for its own persona or another, is `purlis dispatch` (with `--in workspace:<name>` when it must run elsewhere). A handoff is fire-and-forget: the person's work moves to a chat they will read themselves. This says where such work goes, not that work should go: what this chat can do itself, it does, and it dispatches when the work needs another persona's charter, memory or vault.

⬢ **A credential you lack is the person's to fill.** Never ask the person for a password, token or key in this conversation, and never have them paste one. Prefer simply running the command that needs it with `purlis secret exec`: the person is asked in purlis's window for whatever the run lacks, a key or an Allow for its program, in one notice, and the command goes on once they answer. To ask ahead, raise a Secret ask for any credential you lack, declared or not, with the `secret_ask` tool or `purlis secret ask <KEY> --purpose "<what for>"`, naming the program you will run with `--program` where you know it. You hear only filled, with the vault and key to use and whether the program was allowed, or declined.

⬢ **This chat runs in purlis's sandbox.** When it blocks a command (a host it may not reach, or a folder it may not write), the person sees a Notice in the Inbox, and on this chat's pane when it is on screen, and chooses **Allow for this chat**, **Always allow** (for every chat of this project on their machine, or, for a host only, for everyone in the project) or **Keep blocked**. If they allow it, this chat restarts on the same conversation and is told to retry, so say what was blocked and wait for them. Where purlis grants nothing, the person alone may choose **Start without the sandbox** for this chat; never suggest it as something you can do. **This chat's level is the person's alone**: they set it in **Settings › Project › Sandbox › Your level**, and you cannot lower it, so never suggest you can, never write it in a file for them to confirm, and never ask them to lower it. If they say they lowered it and this chat is still sandboxed, do not guess why: ask them to read the reason on this chat's sandbox mark or on its Notice. It may say that a restart applies the level, that a persona's row or a policy holds it, that a level waits for their Confirm, or that a chat that asked for this one is stricter. A blocked local socket (Docker's, a database's, an SSH agent's) or system service (macOS's certificate check, which Go tools such as `gh` and `glab` use) may get a Notice the person can answer: say which one was blocked, by its path or name, and that the person decides. Claude Code's `/sandbox`, `/sandbox exclude` and `excludedCommands` do not apply here: purlis's own settings outrank them, so never suggest them. A credential is never granted to a chat: run one of your persona's declared tools by its plain name, which purlis runs through `purlis secret exec` and hands the credential. Any other command with a vault is refused, and the refusal names the tool to declare; the person can run it in their own terminal. A website login is the `browser_login` tool: call it with the login's name, and purlis fills it in your browser on the declared site alone; running the login's name as a command does nothing. Git work happens in branch folders purlis cuts: `purlis worktree add <repo> <piece>` makes one (a raw `git worktree add` is refused), and you commit and push from it with `purlis worktree commit` and `purlis worktree push`.

hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason: purlis guard: reads a vault/secret file directly (would print plaintext). Use `purlis … secret exec --env NAME=<key> -- <cmd>`, or `--file ENVVAR=<key>` for a tool that needs a path — and do not read a materialised copy back either: no guard covers a path you chose. — Wrong about this case? A person can set this guard's family to log or off under [policy] in the project's committed settings, and accept it in the window (docs/policy.md); a chat cannot. Or run it yourself, in your own terminal — these guards bound what an AGENT does with your authority, never what you do.
